title: About None value not stored to _ in interactive mode
author: xitop
Rosuav
text:
The behaviour you’re looking at can actually be customized. What happens is that sys.displayhook is called with the value, and it’s up to that function to choose what to do. If you wanted to, say, have ALL the values retained as __[-1] and __[-2] etc, you could redefine sys.displayhook to do that.



Python documentation



sys — System-specific parameters and functions
This module provides access to some variables used or maintained by the interpreter and to functions that interact strongly with the interpreter. It is always available. Unless explicitly noted otherwise, all variables are read-only. | This module...





The informal introduction is, as you say, allowed to be a bit incomplete; but I think it would be useful to link to those docs from the section on expression statements. It could be as simple as adding this sentence to the last paragraph:
“This is done by calling sys.displayhook with the value, and can be customized by replacing that function.”

author: jonathandung
text: It should be expected behaviour, or you would lose the last result after printing something using print.
